micro_topic: Unitary features > Governor, CAG, emergency (vs Central Services)
core_fact: Departures from federal principles: Governor appointed by and holding office at the pleasure of the President; a single CAG auditing Union and State accounts; emergency powers converting the federation into a unitary State. Central Services (Union-only cadres) do not touch State autonomy; the All-India Services (Art. 312) do.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The office of the Governor violates the federal principles of the Indian Constitution.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The Central Services violate the federal principles of the Indian Constitution.
statements.true_fact: Central Services work only on Union subjects; the All-India Services are the feature criticised as anti-federal.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General violates the federal principles of the Indian Constitution.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Emergency powers violate the federal principles of the Indian Constitution.

reconstruction.correct_statement: Governor, CAG and emergency powers are unitary features; Central Services are not.
reconstruction.transformation: Central Services confused with All-India Services.
reconstruction.why: Only services that serve States under central control erode autonomy.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Central Services (Union only) vs All-India Services (IAS/IPS/IFoS, Art. 312, serve States, controlled by Centre).

leaf_note: Parliament entering the State List is legislative relations.
micro_topic: Parliament legislating on State List > Arts 249, 252, 253
core_fact: Parliament may legislate on State List subjects: national interest on a Rajya Sabha resolution by 2/3 of members present and voting (Art. 249); national emergency (Art. 250); consent of two or more States (Art. 252); to implement international treaties/agreements (Art. 253); President's Rule (Art. 357). Lok Sabha has no such resolution power.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Parliament can make laws on State List subjects on the request of two or more States.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Parliament can make laws on State List subjects when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting in the national interest.

phrases.phrase: two-thirds of the members present and voting

statements.text: Parliament can make laws on State List subjects to give effect to international agreements.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Parliament can make laws on State List subjects when the Lok Sabha passes a resolution with two-thirds of members present and voting in the national interest.
statements.true_fact: Only the Rajya Sabha (representing States) can pass the Art. 249 resolution.

reconstruction.correct_statement: Arts 249 (RS resolution), 252 (States' request), 253 (treaties) - not a Lok Sabha resolution.
reconstruction.transformation: Rajya Sabha replaced by Lok Sabha.
reconstruction.why: RS is the States' House; only it can transfer a State subject.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: RS special powers: Art. 249 (State List), Art. 312 (new AIS); both need 2/3 present and voting.

micro_topic: Fundamental Duties > 11th duty (Art. 51A(k)) > 86th Amendment 2002
core_fact: The 86th Amendment Act 2002 added Art. 51A(k) - duty of a parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child between 6 and 14 - along with Art. 21A and the new Art. 45.

reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: 86th Amd 2002: Art. 21A + new 45 + 51A(k); RTE Act 2009 in force 1 Apr 2010.

micro_topic: UPSC > central recruiting agency vs constitutional status
core_fact: The UPSC (Art. 315) is the central recruiting agency of India and an independent constitutional body; its recruiting role flows from Art. 320 functions, not from its constitutional status as such.

statements.mechanism: true fact not the one asked

reconstruction.correct_statement: UPSC is the central recruiting agency (Art. 320) and an independent constitutional body (Art. 315); the second does not explain the first.
reconstruction.why: Function comes from Art. 320, not from status.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: UPSC: recruitment (Art. 320) + independence (Arts 316-319); A-R on two features of one body is usually 'not the explanation'.

micro_topic: 73rd Amendment > significance > justiciable Part IX
core_fact: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave PRIs constitutional status in Part IX, shifting them from the non-justiciable DPSP (Art. 40) to justiciable provisions binding the States - hence a landmark in grassroots democracy.

reconstruction.correct_statement: The 73rd Amendment is a landmark because it made PRIs a justiciable constitutional obligation.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: 73rd Amd: Art. 40 (DPSP) converted into binding Part IX; States must hold elections every 5 years.

core_fact: All-India Services (Art. 312) serve both Union and States but are recruited by UPSC and governed by central rules (AIS Act 1951); States cannot dismiss or fully discipline them - hence criticised as violating federalism and State autonomy.

micro_topic: Inter-State Council > Art. 263 vs Rajamannar recommendation
core_fact: Art. 263 (1950) lets the President set up an Inter-State Council for co-ordination; the Rajamannar Committee (1969) strongly urged its creation; it was actually set up in 1990 on Sarkaria's recommendation.

statements.mechanism: true fact not the one asked

reconstruction.correct_statement: Art. 263 provides for an ISC; Rajamannar (1969) later urged its creation - not the reason for the Article.
reconstruction.transformation: Later recommendation offered as cause of an earlier Article.
reconstruction.why: A 1969 report cannot explain a 1950 provision.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: ISC: Art. 263 (1950) -> Rajamannar 1969, ARC 1969 -> Sarkaria 1988 -> set up 1990.

leaf_note: Emergency effects are the classic unitary feature.
micro_topic: National Emergency (Art. 352) > effects on federalism and FRs
core_fact: During a National Emergency: the Centre may give executive directions to any State on any matter (Art. 353(a)); Parliament may legislate on State List (Art. 250); the President may modify distribution of revenues (Art. 354); Art. 19 is suspended (Art. 358, war/external aggression only) and the President may suspend enforcement of other FRs except Arts 20 and 21 (Art. 359, 44th Amendment 1978).

statements.label: A

phrases.phrase: modify the constitutional distribution of finances
phrases.meaning_here: Art. 354, until end of the financial year

statements.text: During a National Emergency the Centre becomes entitled to give executive directions to a State on any matter.

statements.label: C
statements.text: During a National Emergency the President can suspend all the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.
statements.true_fact: The President may suspend enforcement of FRs except Arts 20 and 21 (44th Amendment).

reconstruction.correct_statement: Emergency: Art. 354 finance change and Art. 353 directions - but Arts 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Art. 358 suspends Art. 19 automatically (war/external aggression); Art. 359 suspends enforcement of others except 20 and 21.

reconstruction.why: PIL relaxes locus standi - an activist move.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: PIL: activism, relaxed locus standi, epistolary jurisdiction; Iyer & Bhagwati; first reported: Hussainara Khatoon 1979.
